title: DEC-216: Locale stale-legal gauge counts only active entries; the read sets the RPC context (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Problem**: Review V3: F-10 the DEC-213 gauge counted entries in every lifecycle, so a stale no_fallback field on an archived, deletion_pending or held entry (not revalidatable) would hold the alert open; F-1 the reader never set app.cms_rpc, so forced RLS answered zero rows.
- **Options considered**: (A) count only lifecycle active entries; (B) count every lifecycle (spec-literal); (C) count active plus held.
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier; alert must be actionable) and specified that the read sets and restores the transaction-local RPC context like every protected read. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c DEC-208 paragraph + changelog; dec208 reader, wrapper and pgTAP.
- **Reversibility**: High.

title: PAT-031: Fixtures that hold app.cms_rpc for the whole transaction hide a read that forgets it (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Type**: anti-pattern
- **Confidence**: 0.6 (third instance of a stub/fixture supplying the hoped-for context: S07/08 header, S12 nil-UUID probe, now dec208)
- **Context**: Any new SECURITY DEFINER entry point (platform_api wrapper, service_role RPC, trigger) over forced-RLS cms_ tables.
- **Pattern**: Every entry point needs a context-cleared test: clear app.cms_rpc, call as the real caller role, assert real non-zero rows and that the caller value is restored, plus a negative control (model phase_02_slice_12_fix_template_reads_rpc_context.sql). A suite whose fixtures set the flag globally proves nothing about the entry point. Root scan: grep WIP entry points for set_config(app.cms_rpc).
- **Source**: Review V3 F-1: dec208 locale observability read answered zeros under forced RLS while its 78/78 suite passed.

title: DEC-217: DEC-206 composition-instance read aligned to BE00 collection rules (amends DEC-206) (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Problem**: DEC-206 as recorded said cursor pages of at most 100 with an opaque nextCursor and an order led by region; reviews R3-01/R3-02/R3-04 and V1-02 found that contradicts BE00 collection rules and the CMS-03C-13 precedent, and the 409-versus-400 choice for a bad cursor was never one recorded decision.
- **Options considered**: (A) align to BE00: limit 1-50 default 25, signed keyset cursor (domain cms-03c-instances, shared Vault seal helpers of CMS-03C-13) bound to route, entry, draft revision, sort and user/acting context, at most 24 h, tamper/expiry/cross-context reuse 400, items at most 50, order slot ordinal, position, path, id; web loader follows nextCursor to exhaustion with fail-closed guards (repeated cursor, 20 s budget) and an explicit degraded 503 notice, no row cap; (B) keep DEC-206 as recorded (opaque cursor, pages of 100, 2,000-row loader cap).
- **Decision**: A (root correction after review R3, implemented by lane F4a, verified PROMOTE by review V1). Supersedes the paging text of DEC-206; DEC-206 authority and shape otherwise stand.
- **Downstream**: BE03c rows 182/409/1188-1196 and changelog; FE03 composition page rows; dec206 SQL, contracts, Worker, web loader.
- **Reversibility**: Medium until promotion.

title: DEC-218: Governed recheck isolates per-review failures (counted unavailable, left live, cursor advances) (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Problem**: R3-08 / lane F4b BOUNDARY: BE03c was silent on one review failing inside a cms.governed_review.recheck run; before the fix one failing review aborted the run and pinned the cursor.
- **Options considered**: (A) count the review unavailable, leave it live, advance the cursor; lock timeout or deadlock stays the retryable conflict for the whole run; (B) invalidate the review on any unexpected error (fail-closed, but an internal error would push subjects back to draft); (C) keep aborting the run (one poison review blocks every later review).
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier): safe because CMS-03C-09 step (4) rechecks subject hash, policy basis and every dependency under its locks, so a passed-over live review cannot activate a stale subject; the unavailable count is in the run result. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c Governed review machinery paragraph and changelog; governed-recheck 030100.
- **Reversibility**: High.

title: DEC-219: Locale stale-legal gauge cost bounded by live entries (skip scan); read failures counted and alerted (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Problem**: The dec208 lane cost model (review V3 F-5): the gauge visited every stale row ever appended each minute; cms_locale_variants is append-only, so cost grows without bound, and once a read exceeds the 5,000 ms abort every tick becomes a swallowed warning and the stale legal-field alert input disappears silently.
- **Options considered**: (A) start from active entries and skip-scan the current-row index per (entry, locale) head, plus a failure counter and an alert on five failed reads in ten minutes; (B) keep the query and add only the failure alert; (C) maintain a head table or incremental gauge (new write path).
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier): bounded by live entries x locales (at most 32 each), no new write path, and the alert input can no longer vanish silently. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c DEC-208 paragraph + changelog; dec208 reader SQL and pgTAP; Worker probe counter cms_locale_observability_read_failed_total and the locale_observability_unavailable alert in the composition alert evaluator.
- **Reversibility**: High.

title: PAT-032: Back up untracked WIP before editing it in place (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Type**: anti-pattern
- **Confidence**: 0.5
- **Context**: Lanes edit supabase/migrations-wip/ files in place; those files are untracked, so git cannot restore them.
- **Pattern**: Tar the claimed untracked files into the lane scratch dir before the first in-place edit and record the tar path; take any baseline (snapshot, TAP) BEFORE mutating. Now in lane-rules.md.
- **Source**: DEC-215 squash lane applied edits before its baseline snapshot succeeded and had to rebuild 24 originals byte-exactly from transcripts (verified against a stage manifest).

title: DEC-220: Plain-locale index for the gauge skip scan; read-failure alert per firing, no in-process window (2026-10-22)
text:
- **Problem**: dec208 round 3 measured that lower(locale) cannot be an index condition under forced RLS (lower() is not leakproof), and the DEC-219 five-failures-in-ten-minutes alert was held in Worker process memory, which scheduled firings on fresh isolates never accumulate.
- **Options considered**: (A) ratify INDEX(entry_id, locale, version DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC) and raise locale_observability_unavailable on every failed firing (stateless; delivery dedupes); (B) stored lowercase key column (schema change on an append-only table); (C) keep the in-process window (alert may never fire); (D) durable window state in KV or a Durable Object (new infrastructure).
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier). Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c DEC-208 paragraph + changelog; dec208 indexes migration; Worker probe and composition alert policy (remove the window).
- **Reversibility**: High.

title: DEC-221: Governed lock failures stay retryable conflicts; revocation skips reviews no longer live (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Problem**: Review V4-02: the promoted cms_governed_frozen_status maps any digest error, including 40P01/55P03 from block FOR SHARE waits, to changed, so a deadlock invalidates a healthy review (recheck, decision and activation share it). V4-05: if an activation commits while the revoker waits for the subject lock, the person invalidation updates an activated review, the guard raises CONFLICT and the revocation itself fails.
- **Options considered**: V4-02 (A) forward-patch frozen_status to re-raise lock-class SQLSTATEs and keep mapping genuine digest failures to changed; (B) leave fail-closed. V4-05 (A) re-read under the subject lock and skip a review that is no longer live; (B) lock every grant and tenure row of the owner organization first like the S10 activation; (C) leave (revocation retry succeeds).
- **Decision**: Root chose A and A (implementation tier): BE03b rule 3 already says a lock failure is CONFLICT, and revocation is a security action that must not fail on an unrelated race. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c Governed review machinery + changelog; forward patch of 20261013300400 in a new WIP dir; governed-recheck 030200; tests incl. fault injection and race modules after promotion.
- **Reversibility**: High.

title: DEC-222: Linked-update scan semantics where BE03c was silent (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Problem**: The linked-scan lane implemented AC-212/213 and found six spec-silent points: what a draft revision is, an already-pending head, inactive targets, actor attribution, entry version, audit.
- **Options considered**: draft = current draft revision in derived state draft vs any non-published revision; older pending head gets a newer pending row vs skip; created_by = head creator vs a system actor (none exists; column NOT NULL to auth.users); audit per run vs none (rows self-describing, review invalidation already audited, matching the S11/S12 system jobs).
- **Decision**: Root ratified the lane choices: current draft in derived state draft; newer pending row; inactive target no-op; head created_by; no entry version bump; no audit of its own. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c Linked update paragraph + changelog; linked-scan WIP; review V6.
- **Reversibility**: High until promotion.

title: DEC-223: Governed reviewer authority follows the 03b grant and tenure triggers (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Problem**: R3-07 / V4-12e: the governed reviewer-authority invalidation was wired only to grant revocation; BE03c said governed reviews apply the 03b invalidation rules unchanged, and 03b also invalidates on membership tenure change.
- **Options considered**: (A) mirror the 03b AFTER UPDATE/DELETE triggers on organization_actor_grant and membership_tenure (tenure passes a null capability, the new person too when an update changes it), each re-asking the unmodified reader so a still-authorized reviewer is spared; (B) rely only on lazy discovery by activation recount.
- **Decision**: A (root; it is the stated 03b rule, made explicit in BE03c). Implemented in governed-recheck 030200; review V4 confirmed semantics.
- **Downstream**: BE03c Reviewer-authority invalidation paragraph; governed-recheck triggers and tests; race modules R-1..R-4 after promotion.
- **Reversibility**: Medium.

title: PAT-033: Real-API suites share one committed database; scope claims and digests to your own world (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Type**: anti-pattern
- **Confidence**: 0.5
- **Context**: pnpm db:api-test runs every tests/postgrest apispec sequentially on one database and the suites COMMIT fixtures; global sweeps (CMS-03B-20 publication, CMS-03C-19 governed activation) claim every due row.
- **Pattern**: A suite that sleeps and then ticks a global sweep must assert only on its own world rows and digests; another suite may leave near-future schedules that fall due during the sleep. Verify a suspected interference by running the file alone on a fresh reset before touching product code. Also: a test that switches the caller must restore it in afterEach/finally, or one failure cascades into the next test (seen as 403 where 503 was expected).
- **Source**: Canonical db:verify after the Slice 12 promotion: S11 sweep-outcomes failed in the full run and passed alone 3/3; two S12 apispec 503 failures were a session-restore cascade.

title: DEC-224: Publication commands lock the revision pattern dependencies FOR SHARE at position 3 (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Problem**: The first canonical run of the DEC-199 publication race showed cms_publish_revision (and schedule/execute) never lock the PatternVersion rows the pattern provider reads, while CMS-03C-09 activation takes the lineage active row FOR UPDATE; a pin could be superseded between the provider check and the commit.
- **Options considered**: (A) lock the live pattern root and nested rows FOR SHARE in ascending id at position 3 in the publication review-lock helpers (schedule, publish, execute); (B) also lock at submit and decision; (C) rely on the provider check alone.
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier): publication is where a stale pin would become public; submit and decision are fail-safe because publication rechecks every pin and refuses a stale one. Forward fix in race-fixes WIP; BE03c lock-order row added. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: BE03c Slice 12 lock order + changelog; race-fixes migrations 20261023100000/100100; dec199 race; S11 publication races rerun.
- **Reversibility**: Medium.

title: DEC-225: Canonical race mode does not assert the protected primary checkout path (2026-10-23)
text:
- **Problem**: Review V9-03: the converted Slice 12 race modules keep assert.notEqual(root, /home/rob/Projects/WeJammin) in canonical mode, so after merge a canonical pnpm db:verify run from the owner primary checkout fails four modules by design.
- **Options considered**: (A) drop the checkout-path assert in canonical mode only (the canonical runner targets the canonical disposable stack anyway), keep it in ALT mode; (B) keep it everywhere and require canonical runs from a worktree; (C) remove it everywhere.
- **Decision**: Root chose A (implementation tier): the assert is a lane-safety rule for ALT diagnostics, not a product rule. Owner may override.
- **Downstream**: infra/database-races/canonical-mode.mjs, the four modules, the canonical-mode contract test, README.
- **Reversibility**: High.
